The Stranger.text: Baldur (Old Norse: Baldr, Nordic: ᛒᚨᛚᛞᚢᚱ), also known as Baldur Odinson (Translation: Baldur, Son of Odin), and also known as the Stranger, was the Norse Aesir God of Light, Peace, Beauty, and Goodness as well as Prince of Asgard.

Dragon Hræzlyr.text: Hræzlyr is a male Dragon and a boss in God of War (2018). Hræzlyr is a male Dragon that lives in the Heart of the Mountain, the highest peak in Midgard and a former Jötnar residence. When Kratos and his son Atreus were travelling through the mountain's interior to reach the summit, Hræzlyr attacked them on their way up. After a brief fight, the Dragon retreated towards the exterior.

Magni and Modi.text: Magni (Old Norse: Mágni, Nordic: ᛗᚨᚷᚾᛁ), also known as Magni Thorson (Translation: Magni, Son of Thor), was the eldest son of Thor and Járnsaxa as well as grandson of Odin and Fjörgyn, nephew of Týr, Heimdall and Baldur, older half-brother of Modi and Thrúd. He is the tertiary antagonist of the God of War (2018) game.

Rota.text: Róta is a Valkyrie introduced in God of War (2018). She is one of the nine Valkyries who have been cursed by Odin to remain in a corporal form, eventually driving them to insanity. As she became too dangerous, Róta eventually found herself sealed away by the Valkyrie Queen in Helheim. She is nevertheless freed by Kratos and Atreus after they engaged and defeated her physical form.

Gondul.text: Göndul is a Valkyrie introduced in God of War (2018). She is one of the nine Valkyries who have been cursed by Odin to remain in a corporal form, eventually driving them to insanity. As she became too dangerous, Göndul eventually found herself sealed away by the Valkyrie Queen in Muspelheim.

Sigrun, Queen of the Valkyries.text: Sigrún is the Valkyrie Queen introduced in God of War (2018). She is one of the nine Valkyries who have been cursed into insanity by Odin. Although the incredible amount of power she possesses allowed her to resist much longer than her sisters, she inevitably lost herself as well. She is nevertheless freed by Kratos and Atreus after they engaged and defeated her physical form in a long and difficult battle.

Gná, Queen of the Valkyries.text: Gná (Old Norse: gnɑ) was the Vanir Goddess of Swift Travel, and Freya's former handmaiden. She is introduced in God of War Ragnarök as the new Queen of the Valkyries, since Sigrún regained her freedom following her defeat at the hands of Kratos and Atreus, three years ago.

Graphorn Lord.text: A named Graphorn, The Lord of the Shore, is acquired as a mount by completing San Bakar's Trial towards the end of the main story. The same den can be revisited afterwards to get more Graphorns (one per visit). Due to their aggressive nature, Graphorns are more difficult to capture than other beasts. They must be weakened by fighting before they can be pulled into the Nab-Sack.

True Corrupted Monk.text: The Corrupted Monk (破戒僧, Depraved Monk) is a mandatory Boss with one Deathblow counter. She's an illusion that guards the entrance of the Wedding Cave Door, where the Shelter Stone is enshrined. As an illusion, she's vulnerable to Snap Seeds which will deplete a large portion of her Vitality bar and damage her Posture too, staggering her in the process. Only three will have effect on her though.

Mister Negative.text: He was the founder and owner of the F.E.A.S.T. shelter. At the same time, he was also secretly the ruthless leader of a criminal group known as the Inner Demons and possesses the ability to harness a form of negative energy at will. He had a personal vendetta against Mayor Norman Osborn, which led him to terrorize the city.

Electro and Vulture.text: Born around 1979,[a] in Endicott, New York, Max Dillon was involved in an unspecified accident which granted him the ability to absorb electricity and deploy it in destructive blasts. Becoming the super-criminal Electro, Dillon had several encounters with Peter Parker's Spider-Man over the years. At one point, he perpetrated a killing spree for which Spider-Man was blamed by J.

Rhino and Scorpion.text: After spending years incarcerated in the Raft, the armored brute is released by Doctor Octopus, who makes him part of his supervillain group the Sinister Six. After being locked up and sent to the Raft, he escaped again during a prison transfer, becoming an enforcer for Roxxon. Aleksei Sytsevich was born around 1977[a] in Irkutsk, Russia.

Doctor Octopus.text: A brilliant scientist with an expertise in prosthetics, Octavius built a neural interface capable of controlling robotic arms. He co-founded the megacorporation Oscorp alongside Norman Osborn, before parting ways due to disagreements over GR-27 (Devil's Breath).

Backpacks (55).text: Collections is a menu option that can be used by players to review various items of interest that they have acquired over the course of Marvel's Spider-Man. Tokens are resources that are required to craft gadgets, suits, and suit mods. There are six different types of tokens: These are episode archives of J. Jonah Jameson's radio show called Just the Facts.

Sandman.text: Flint was born in 1976. He had a poor background, growing up in poverty. At some point after Flint became the super criminal, Sandman, Peter Parker (going by the alias Spider-Man) kept a vial containing fragments of his memories. Flint also originally planned a robbery at F.E.A.S.T., until May Parker warded him off peacefully, making him realize the error of his ways when he saw poor people like himself.

Kraven the Hunter.text: Afflicted with an inoperable cancer that sealed his fate, Kraven sought to perpetuate his ancestors' traditions by seeking a glorious death at the hands of a worthy predator, leading him to his last Great Hunt in New York City. He ruthlessly hunted down and killed many infamous supervillains, such as Scorpion, Vulture, Electro, and Shocker.

The Lizard.text: He is first mentioned in Marvel's Spider-Man, when Spider-Man finds a backpack containing a vial of his blood, before making his on-screen debut in the mid-credits scene of Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales. He returns in Marvel's Spider-Man 2, not only as a prominent character, but as a major antagonist when Kraven the Hunter forcibly transforms him back into the Lizard before being cured by Spider-Man. Dr.

Bloater (Pittsburgh hotel).text: Bloaters are the fourth, rarest, and one of the most dangerous stages of the infected in The Last of Us and The Last of Us Part II. They take a few years to develop and reach this stage after exposure to the Cordyceps brain infection. Bloaters are incredibly strong and physically imposing infected that are covered in thick fungus that effectively acts as armor plates.

Abby vs. Ellie (theater).text: Abigail "Abby" Anderson is the playable dual protagonist of The Last of Us Part II and a playable character in the No Return mode. Abby was a member of the original group of Fireflies based in Salt Lake City. Her life was broken by tragedy when Joel Miller killed her father Jerry Anderson.

Journal Entries.text: Ellie's journal is an artifact that is found during the "Jackson" chapter in The Last of Us Part II. It is an old journal owned by Ellie. Here she draws and writes her thoughts throughout the game. Ellie's journal can be found in her house on a desk close to her jacket. It is automatically picked up when she leaves to go on patrol with Dina.

Safes.text: Safes are item caches that can be found in the The Last of Us and The Last of Us Part II. They contain supplies abandoned by people during the initial outbreak or stashed during later conflicts. They require a combination to open, which can be found on certain Artifacts or in the environment. Safes can hold ammo, crafting supplies, parts, and even Training Manuals.

Workbenches.text: A workbench is used in The Last of Us and in The Last of Us Part II to upgrade firearms to make them more powerful. To upgrade them, parts are needed, as well as tools upgrades in the first game. As Joel acquires weapons, tools, and parts, he can use them to make his weapons more powerful, such as faster reloading and adding a second gun holsters.

Demon King Ganondorf.text: Notably, as Ganon is revealed to be the endless reincarnation of Demise's hatred from Skyward Sword, and that villain himself is a humanoid, Ganondorf much more closely resembles him.

Shrines (152).text: Shortly after founding Hyrule, King Rauru and Queen Sonia created the Shrines of Light to protect the kingdom from monsters. The shrines sealed the monsters away, making them unable to be resurrected by the Blood Moon, or by any other means.

Lightroots (120).text: Lightroots are structures that are located in The Depths, and are situated directly below Shrines on the surface (with the exception of Turakawak Shrine, as the Kawakarut Lightroot is slightly off). They act as mini-Skyview Towers, revealing a small portion of the map while also creating a Fast Travel point when activated.

Griffin (The Beast of White Orchard).text: While the quest objectives indicate that you must ask the relevant individuals for help locating Geralt's intended goal this is not actually the case. If you happen to know the locations or happen upon the patrol that was attacked or where the buckthorn is growing, you can simply go to those locations. This bypasses some interesting story parts and may affect some side quests so it is not recommended.

The Crones.text: The Crones, also called the Ladies of the Wood, are three witches who live in a cabin in the swamps of Velen. Legend suggests the three are sisters and the daughters of the original "Lady of the Wood", also known as "She-Who-Knows". They are named Brewess, Weavess, and Whispess.

Shrines (120).text: After the Sheikah helped to seal away Calamity Ganon, they built the Ancient Shrines to serve as training grounds for the hero as he prepared for the revival of Calamity Ganon. There are initially 120 Ancient Shrines scattered throughout Hyrule Kingdom.

Cyberpsycho Sightings (17).text: This job mainly acts as a tracker for the 17 cyberpsycho jobs. Once all of them have been completed, Regina will call V to have a meeting in person, with her comments based on if you had managed to keep them all alive or not before she gives you your reward. If none are killed, she is very grateful, as she is helping them get therapy to further understand their condition.

Sacred Tears (12).text: Blessing of the Erdtree, worshiped in the churches of all lands; this is but a faint vestige. Increases the potency of a Sacred Flask's restorative effects. (Can be used after resting at a site of grace.) During the age of the Erdtree, these tears were used to spread the faith, for theirs was once a certain blessing.

Rampages (35).text: Rampages are challenges started via collectibles in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. There are a total of 35 Rampages located all around Vice City, appearing as a rotating white skull pickup item, which the player must find and collect while on foot and not in an active mission to trigger the challenge. If the player fails a Rampage, they are allowed to immediately restart it at its original spawn point.

Treasures.text: Collectible items are present throughout the Resident Evil titles. In earlier games, these were only items that were unlocked after completing the game under certain conditions (e.g. an S rank, a higher difficulty or beating it a set number of times), but were none-the-less collected as a means of proving one's achievements, like the rocket launcher in the first Resident Evil.

Unusual Gems (24).text: The city of Riften has two people capable of handling this task: Maul, an associate of Maven Black-Briar, and Vex, a member of the Thieves Guild. After the appraisal, it is revealed that a total of 24 Stones of Barenziah exist, which activates the quest "No Stone Unturned." The stones are quest items of 0.5 weight and worth 200 , and they cannot be removed from the inventory until the entire set is obtained.

Meteorite house.text: This location is situated east of Brandywine Drop and north of Roanoke Valley. The Meteor House is a cabin on a cliff that overlooks Roanoke Valley in Roanoke Ridge, New Hanover. This point of interest features a stone cottage and a small outhouse behind it. Surrounding the house are things such as a shovel, a bundle of firewood, barrels and other gardening tools. The property is encircled by a wooden fence.
